features.name: It Was Me All Along
features.flavor: After everything you've been through together, you twist the blade and make the pain extra personal.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: If you are disguised as a creature the target knew using your I'm No Threat ability, this ability deals extra damage equal to three times your Agility score.

At the start of each of your turns, you can forgo gaining insight to create 1d6 clones of yourself in unoccupied adjacent spaces. A clone acts on your turn and uses your statistics, except they have 1 Stamina. They are affected by any conditions and effects on you, and last until the start of your next turn. A clone doesn't have insight and can't use the Careful Observation ability, the Umbral Form feature, or any triggered actions. On their turn, a clone has a move action, a maneuver, and a main action that they can use only to make a free strike. While making a free strike, a clone must choose targets that you or another clone aren't also striking.

Outside of combat, you can have one clone active for every 2 Victories you have. If a clone is destroyed, you must wait 1 hour before creating another one.
Your Might and Reason scores each increase to 5.

You have an epic resource called command. Each time you finish a respite, you gain command equal to the XP you gain. You can spend command on your abilities as if it were focus.

Additionally, whenever you or any ally uses an ability to deal rolled damage to a creature marked by you, you can spend 1 command as a free triggered action to increase the power roll outcome for that target by one tier. Whenever an enemy marked by you makes an ability roll, you can spend 1 command as a free triggered action to decrease the power roll outcome by one tier.
Command remains until you spend it.
You gain one exploration, interpersonal, or intrigue perk of your choice.
You gain one skill of your choice.
When you gain focus at the start of each of your turns during combat, you gain 4 focus instead of 3.

You have mastered the entirety of possible strategies and tactics. Whenever you or any ally makes an ability roll against a target marked by you, the character making the roll can roll three dice and choose which two to use.

Additionally, whenever an ally uses a heroic ability that targets one or more creatures marked by you, they spend 2 fewer of their Heroic Resource on that ability (minimum 1).

You command any room you walk into. While you are present during a negotiation, each hero with you treats their Renown as 2 higher than usual. Additionally, each hero with you during a combat encounter has a double edge on tests made to stop combat and start a negotiation.

While in your presence or working according to your plans, each of your allies gains an edge on tests using any skill from the intrigue skill group. Additionally, you can use the Lead skill to assist another creature with any test made using a skill from the intrigue group.

At the Director's discretion, you and your allies can use skills from the intrigue skill group to attempt research or reconnaissance during a negotiation instead of outside of a negotiation.

You have drilled with a broad array of arms and armor, and have developed techniques to optimize their use. You can use and gain the benefits of two kits, including both their signature abilities. Whenever you would choose or change one kit, you can choose or change your second kit as well. See Chapter 6: Kits for more information. (*Quick Build:* Shining Armor, Sniper.)

If both kits grant you the same benefit, you take one or the other and can't change your choice until you finish a respite. (This usually means taking the higher of two bonuses.)
For example, if you take the Shining Armor and Sniper kits, you gain the following benefits overall:
- Stamina Bonus: +12 per echelon
- Stability Bonus: +1
- Melee Damage Bonus: +2/+2/+2
- Ranged Damage Bonus: +0/+0/+4
- Speed Bonus: +1
- Ranged Distance Bonus: +10
- Disengage Bonus: +1
- You can use the Patient Shot and Protective Attack signature abilities.
Kit signature abilities have their kit's bonuses already applied, which might require you to adjust the bonuses of the signature abilities you gain from a kit. For example, you might take the Martial Artist kit, which gives a melee weapon damage bonus of +2/+2/+2, and the Mountain kit, which gives a melee weapon damage bonus of +0/+0/+4. If you choose to use the Mountain kit's damage bonus, then the Battle Grace signature ability from the Martial Artist kit loses the +2/+2/+2 bonus from that kit, reducing its usual 5/8/11 damage for its tier 1, tier 2, and tier 3 outcomes to 3/6/9. It then gains the +0/+0/+4 of the Mountain kit to deal 3/6/13 damage.

At the start of a combat encounter or some other stressful situation tracked in combat rounds (as determined by the Director), you gain focus equal to your Victories. At the start of each of your turns during combat, you gain 2 focus.

Additionally, the first time each combat round that you or any ally damages a creature marked by you (see Mark below), you gain 1 focus. The first time in a combat round that any ally within 10 squares of you uses a heroic ability, you gain 1 focus.
You lose any remaining focus at the end of the encounter.

Though you can't gain focus outside of combat, you can use your heroic abilities and effects that cost focus without spending it. Whenever you use an ability or effect outside of combat that costs focus, you can't use that same ability or effect outside of combat again until you earn 1 or more Victories or finish a respite.

When you use an ability outside of combat that lets you spend unlimited focus on its effect, you can use it as if you had spent an amount of focus equal to your Victories. (Such abilities aren't part of the core rules for the tactician, but they might appear in future products.)

Many of the tactician's abilities grant allies extra movement, damage, and actions. But what's happening in the fiction to allow this? The tactician is an incredible strategist and inspiring leader who is quick to give commands and inspiration that causes their allies to act. The tactician can quickly read the battlefield, analyze enemies, and then bark orders and encouragement that pushes their allies to greatness. Many of the names of the tactician's abilities are the actual commands they give their friends!
Each kit from your Field Arsenal feature grants you a signature ability. Signature abilities can be used at will.
You know how to focus the attention of your allies as you push them toward victory. You have the following ability.

features.name: Mark
features.flavor: You draw your allies' attention to a specific foe—with devastating effect.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect:
The target is marked by you until the end of the encounter, until you are dying, or until you use this ability again. You can willingly end your mark on a creature (no action required), and if another tactician marks a creature, your mark on that creature ends. When a creature marked by you is reduced to 0 Stamina, you can use a free triggered action to mark a new target within distance.
You can initially mark only one creature using this ability, though other tactician abilities allow you to mark additional creatures at the same time. The mastermind tactical doctrine's Anticipation feature allows you to target additional creatures with this ability starting at 5th level.
While a creature marked by you is within your line of effect, you and allies within your line of effect gain an edge on power rolls made against that creature. Additionally, whenever you or any ally uses an ability to deal rolled damage to a creature marked by you, you can spend 1 focus to gain one of the following benefits as a free triggered action:
- The ability deals extra damage equal to twice your Reason score.
- The creature dealing the damage can spend a Recovery.
- The creature dealing the damage can shift up to a number of squares equal to your Reason score.
- If you damage a creature marked by you with a melee ability, the creature is taunted by you until the end of their next turn.
You can't gain more than one benefit from the same trigger.

Your encyclopedic knowledge of the history of battle lets you apply that knowledge to current challenges. While you are present, each hero with you treats the Discover Lore project related to a war or battle as one category cheaper. This makes projects seeking common lore free, but such projects still require a respite activity to complete. (See Chapter 12: Downtime Projects for more information.)

Additionally, if you have 24 hours or more before a combat encounter or negotiation, and you have one or more clues or rumors regarding the encounter or negotiation, you can make a Reason test as a respite activity. The following test outcomes apply to a combat encounter:
effects.tier1: The Director tells you the number of creatures in the encounter.
effects.tier2: The Director tells you the number and level of the creatures in the encounter.
effects.tier3: The Director tells you the tier 2 outcome information, and when the encounter begins, all enemies are surprised.

effects.tier2: The Director gives you one motivation for an NPC in the negotiation.

Warfare is as old as civilization—and perhaps even older. As battle became ever more complex, military leaders invented tactical doctrine, outlining how combatants should be structured, used, and deployed. Doctrine can be learned at war colleges passing on ancient martial traditions, or directly through blood and sweat on the battlefield. Whatever path brought you to your mastery of historically proven tactics, you choose a tactical doctrine from the following options, each of which grants you a skill. (*Quick Build:* Vanguard and the Intimidate skill.)
Your tactical doctrine is your subclass, and your choice of doctrine determines many of the features you'll gain as you gain new levels.

Abilities like Guest Star, Missed Cue, and Twist at the End allow the auteur to rewrite bits of what happens in the battle by temporarily removing creatures from an encounter, bringing people back to life, or causing a new ally to appear. These abilities and features are no more powerful than any other, but they're narratively different from shooting rays of fire or swinging a sword.

This is because, uniquely among all the subclasses in *Draw Steel*, the auteur knows that the combat encounter playing out at your table is really a story being told sometime later, probably in a tavern.
When the auteur uses these abilities, they are changing that story. They rewrite stories to make them more dramatic in the telling. What *actually* happened is a matter of some debate. Even the people who were there don't agree on exactly what took place. How people *remember* it is what's important!
This is pretty weird, but also very fun. If it's too weird for you or your table, you could always interpret those abilities as a kind of magic. A school of conjuring that really does change the battlefield, which the auteur merely *flavors* as rewriting the story.

As a respite activity, you can scribe a notice of your arrival (such as a calling card or a formal letter) addressed to an enemy. You can deliver the notice to the target personally if you are in the same general area, send it by courier, or leave it in a covert location for the target to find. You can have only one notice active at a time.

The Director determines when the target receives your notice. When the target receives the notice, they become alarmed and take desperate measures to stop you. The Director gains 1 additional Malice per combat round during encounters involving the target. The heroes start each such encounter with 2 additional hero tokens (Chapter 1: The Basics). While the bond is active, all heroes present treat their Renown as 2 higher than usual for the purpose of entering into a negotiation with the bonded NPC.

The Director can award the heroes 1 hero token to make you infamous among the group of creatures instead, and preventing you from forming this bond. Until you take action to improve your reputation, all heroes present take a bane on tests made to interact with creatures in the group using skills from the interpersonal skill group. You can still use your Scene Partner feature to find allies within the group.
You gain one interpersonal, lore, or supernatural perk of your choice. See Chapter 7: Perks.

At the start of an encounter, choose one creature within your line of effect. You have a double edge on power rolls made against or in competition with that creature. The chosen creature also has a double edge on power rolls made against or in competition with you. If the chosen creature is reduced to 0 Stamina, you can choose a new foil at the start of the next combat round.

If you aren't surprised at the start of an encounter, you can choose one enemy within your line of effect who is not a leader or solo creature. The Director temporarily removes the chosen creature from the encounter. The chosen creature enters the encounter at the start of the second combat round. You must earn 3 Victories before you can use this feature again.
You have the following performance abilities, which are usable with your Routines feature.

features.name: "Fire Up the Night"
features.flavor: Maybe you and I ♪ We can still bring the light!♪
features.target: Self and each ally in the area

effects.name: Effect

features.name: "Never-Ending Hero"
features.flavor: And toniiight we can truly say ♪ They will alllways find a way!♪
features.target: Self and each ally in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: While this performance is active, each target who starts their turn dying while in the area gains an edge on power rolls and ignores the effects of bleeding until the end of their turn.
Your Agility and Presence scores each increase to 3.
You can ask the Director for two clues regarding an upcoming encounter or negotiation. One of the clues can be false.
By bragging, intimidating, leading, or lying, you attempt to spread one piece of information into the local area. Make a Presence test:
effects.tier2: Your information reaches the nearest populated area of town size or larger. You and each ally present when you make the test gain an edge on Presence tests in that area until one of you spends a Recovery.
effects.tier3: Your information reaches the nearest populated area of town size or larger, plus the next closest such population. You and allies present for your test gain an edge on Presence tests made in those areas until you start your next respite.

effects.effect: You can ask the Director for three rumors regarding the area you're in or an area you plan on entering before your next respite. One of the rumors can be false.

You have more ways of getting the most drama out of a situation. Choose two of the following events to add to the events that grant you drama during battle:

- Whenever a creature rolls a natural 2 on a power roll, you gain 2 drama.
- The first time the Director deals damage to a hero using a Villain action or an ability that costs Malice, you gain 2 drama.
- The first time a hero unwillingly falls 5 or more squares, you gain 2 drama.
- The first time a hero deals damage with 3 surges, you gain 2 drama.
- Whenever a hero spends their last Recovery, you gain 2 drama.
Alternatively, you can forgo choosing a new event to choose one event you already have (including an event gained with this feature). Whenever the chosen event grants you drama, you gain 1 additional drama.
You gain one perk of your choice.
You gain one skill of your choice. See Skills in Chapter 9: Tests.

Once on each of your turns, you can use a free maneuver to exchange words with a target of your current performance, other than yourself. The target can spend a Recovery to gain temporary Stamina equal to their recovery value.

Once on each of your turns, you can use a free maneuver to change one condition affecting a creature within distance of your Dramatic Monologue ability. Choose one of the following conditions on the target: bleeding, frightened, prone, slowed, or taunted. You change that condition to another of those conditions, maintaining the duration and origin of the original condition. A target who is no longer prone can stand up.
You can maintain two performances at a time using your Routines feature.

Once on each of your turns while the target of your Foil feature is adjacent to you, you can use a free maneuver to exchange words with them. Make an opposed Presence test with the target. Whoever gets the higher result can make a free strike, which deals psychic damage instead of its usual damage.
You have the following performance ability, which is usable with your Routines feature.

features.name: We Can't Be Upstaged!
features.flavor: Swordplay so graceful it looks like you all practiced this.
features.target: Self and each ally in the area

effects.name: Effect

features.target: Self and each ally in the area

Each of your characteristic scores increases by 1, to a maximum of 4.

You have the following performance abilities, which are usable with your Routines feature.

features.name: Moonlight Sonata
features.flavor: Music pours out of your heart, filling the area with the utmost delicacy and without damper.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: While this performance is active, each target who is dead can choose to continue taking turns after death. On each of their turns, a target can move and use either a main action or a maneuver, but can't spend Recoveries or use triggered actions. At the end of the encounter, each target who chose to take turns this way turns to dust and blows away.

features.name: Radical Fantasia
features.flavor: 𝅘𝅥𝅮♪Viras, my Viras, will you hold their hands as they cryyy—aaaiigh?♪
features.target: Self and each ally in the area

effects.name: Effect

Whenever a creature within distance of your Dramatic Monologue ability makes a power roll, you can spend 1 drama as a free triggered action to use Dramatic Monologue, targeting only one creature.

Choose one of your signature abilities and name it after yourself. You always have this ability available, even if it is sourced from a kit you switch out. Whenever you use this ability, you gain an edge and 1 surge that you can use only on this ability.

effects.tier1: The target takes a bane on ability rolls (save ends).
effects.tier2: The target has a double bane on ability rolls (save ends).
effects.tier3: The target has a double bane on power rolls (save ends).

effects.name: Effect

features.flavor: You narrate the tension of the scene and put all hope into your protagonist to turn things around.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The target gains 3 of their Heroic Resource, has a double edge on a power roll of their choice made during their next turn, is no longer slowed or weakened if they were before, and can immediately take their turn after yours if they have not taken their turn already this round.

features.name: Expert Fencer
features.flavor: If you can land the strike, the crowd goes wild.

effects.tier3: 28 + A damage; M < STRONG, bleeding (save ends)

features.flavor: No, no. You don't die until the sequel.

effects.name: Effect

You are empowered by your audience, near and far. You can't be made frightened, and if you are prone, you can stand up as a free maneuver.

items.name: Angry Beehive

stats.name: Immunity

features.name: Power Roll + 2:

effects.effect: The blades are concealed inside the column, which remains motionless until triggered.

effects.name: Spiked Flails
effects.effect: Instead of blades, the column is affixed with heavy spiked balls attached by long chains. The **Whirling Flails** ability replaces **Spinning Blades**.

features.name: Whirling Flails
features.trigger: A creature or object moves within distance of the column.

effects.effect: Allies who shift don't trigger the column. A creature observing an ally shift this way can make an **Intuition test** to shift in imitation of their movements.

effects.tier1: The creature triggers the column and the column's ability gains an edge.
effects.tier3: The creature doesn't trigger the column.

items.name: Dart Trap
items.flavor: A concealed dart thrower hurls missiles at short range.

stats.name: Direction
stats.value: The dart trap fires in a fixed direction.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a dart trap can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature triggers the trap and is targeted by it.
effects.tier2: The trap is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The trap is deactivated and doesn't trigger.

effects.effect: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The **Dart** ability.

features.name: Dart
features.trigger: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Poison Darts
effects.effect: The darts are tipped with poison. Any creature who takes damage from a dart also takes 1d6 poison damage at the start of each of their turns (save ends).

effects.name: Large Darts
effects.effect: Larger, heavier darts impart kinetic force to the trap's attack. A target of the **Dart** ability is pushed 1 square on a tier 1 outcome, 2 squares on a tier 2 outcome, or 3 squares on a tier 3 outcome.

effects.name: Gatling Darts
effects.effect: The dart trap is equipped with multiple barrels to launch darts at a high rate of fire. The **Dart** ability loses the Ranged and Strike and takes the Area keyword, its area becomes a 5 x 1 line within 1, and it deals an extra 1d6 damage.
The dart trap is hidden until triggered or detected.

items.name: Pillar
items.flavor: This stone pillar can be toppled onto unsuspecting foes with the right amount of damage or a well-engineered trigger mechanism.
items.size: One square that can't be moved through

stats.name: Direction
stats.value: The pillar topples in a preset direction.

effects.effect: The pillar's linked trigger must be deactivated.
The pillar is destroyed, or a pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The **Toppling Pillar** ability.

features.name: Toppling Pillar
features.target: Each creature and object in the area
features.trigger: The pillar is destroyed, or a pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The area is difficult terrain.

effects.name: Metal Pillar
effects.effect: The pillar is made of metal, has 9 Stamina, and deals 1d6 extra damage.

effects.name: Multiple Pillars
effects.effect: Multiple pillars can be used to represent a larger toppling object such as a wall. If triggered by destruction, all individual pillars need to be destroyed before the object falls.

items.name: Portcullis
items.flavor: A portcullis is hidden in the ceiling of a passage or choke point, waiting to drop when activated.
items.size: The area of the corridor to be blocked

stats.name: Typical Space
stats.value: 2 x 1-square area, up to a 4 x 2-square area

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a portcullis can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature triggers the portcullis and is affected as if in its area.
effects.tier2: The portcullis is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The portcullis is deactivated and doesn't trigger.

effects.effect: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The **Heavy Gate** ability.

features.name: Heavy Gate
features.target: Each creature and object in the area
features.trigger: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Special
effects.effect: The area of this ability is the area directly beneath the portcullis when it falls.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The portcullis blocks movement from one side of it to the other. A target slid by the portcullis ends up on one side of it or the other (choose randomly). The portcullis must be manually reset.
The portcullis is hidden until triggered or detected.

items.name: Pressure Plate
items.flavor: This mechanism acts as a trigger for another linked mechanism, and is skillfully hidden from view in the floor.

stats.name: Typical Space
stats.value: One square, up to a 4 x 4-square area

stats.name: Link
stats.value: A pressure plate is linked to another mechanism that it activates when triggered.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a pressure plate can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature triggers the pressure plate.
effects.tier2: The pressure plate is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The pressure plate is deactivated and doesn't trigger.

effects.effect: The pressure plate is calibrated to be triggered by creatures or objects of a particular size. The pressure plate triggers when a creature or object of the appropriate size enters its area.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The linked mechanism is activated. A pressure plate automatically resets and can be triggered repeatedly.

effects.name: Tripwire
effects.effect: The pressure plate is a tripwire, which can trigger once and must be manually reset. A concealed tripwire can be discovered with an **easy Intuition test**.
The pressure plate is hidden until triggered or detected.

items.name: Pulley
items.flavor: A counterweighted pulley system can be used to quickly ascend to the top of a wall, scaffold, tower, or other structure.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a pulley can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier2: The pulley is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The pulley is deactivated and doesn't trigger.

effects.effect: A creature adjacent to the pulley uses a maneuver to release the pulley.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The triggering creature is lifted to the top of the structure the pulley is attached to. The pulley must be manually reset.
A creature adjacent to the pulley can climb its ropes with an **easy Agility test** to ascend to the top of the structure it's attached to.

effects.name: Looped Chain
effects.effect: Instead of a rope and pulley, the system uses a counterweighted looped chain. A looped chain automatically resets and can be triggered repeatedly.

items.name: Ram
items.flavor: A heavy wooden ram drops down or swings into the fray, crushing all in its path.
items.size: Any area; the area can't be moved through

stats.name: Typical Space
stats.value: 1 x 3-square area or a 2 x 2-square area

stats.name: Direction
stats.value: One side of the ram is defined as the front.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a ram can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature triggers the ram and is affected as if in its space.
effects.tier2: The ram is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The ram is deactivated and doesn't trigger.

effects.effect: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The **Ram** ability.

features.name: Ram
features.target: Each creature and object in the area
features.trigger: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.

effects.name: Special
effects.effect: The area of this ability is the path the ram moves through from its starting position.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: A target slid by the ram ends up on one side of it or the other (choose randomly). The ram must be manually reset.

effects.name: Stone
effects.effect: The ram is made of stone, has 6 Stamina per square, and deals an extra 1d3 damage.

effects.name: Metal
effects.effect: The ram is made of metal, has 9 Stamina per square, and deals an extra 1d6 damage.

effects.name: Repeating
effects.effect: The ram automatically resets at the start of each round.

effects.name: Rapid Repeating
effects.effect: The ram automatically resets at the start of each turn.

effects.name: Multiple Rams
effects.effect: Multiple rams can be used to represent a larger mechanism, such as a stack of tumbling logs.
The ram is hidden until triggered or detected.

items.name: Switch
items.flavor: Set into any surface, this mechanism acts as a trigger for another linked mechanism.

stats.name: Link
stats.value: A switch is linked to another mechanism that it activates when triggered.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a switch can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier2: The switch is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The switch is deactivated and doesn't trigger.

effects.effect: A creature adjacent to the switch uses a maneuver to trigger it.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The linked mechanism is activated. A switch automatically resets and can be triggered repeatedly.

effects.name: Concealed
effects.effect: The switch is hidden.

items.name: Holy Idol
items.flavor: An empowering monument to a higher power enables a villain's machinations.

effects.effect: The holy idol must be completely destroyed.

At the start of each round while the holy idol is intact, the Director gains a d6 that lasts until the end of the round. When a Director-controlled creature deals or takes damage, the Director can roll the d6 to increase the damage the creature deals or reduce the damage the creature takes by an amount equal to the roll (to a minimum of 2 damage). If multiple idols are in play, only one d6 can be applied to a single instance of damage.

items.name: Psionic Shard
items.flavor: A massive humming crystal makes the air around it feel thick.

effects.effect: The psionic shard must be completely destroyed.
A psionic shard is attuned to one side in an encounter. While a psionic shard is intact, any damage dealt to each ally of the shard in the encounter is halved.

features.name: Psionic Pulse
features.trigger: The shard is destroyed.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The shard releases a shockwave channeled through each creature affected by Psionic Barrier. Each ally in the encounter is dazed until the end of their next turn.

items.name: Tree of Might
items.flavor: A gnarled tree has unearthed roots that writhe and curl.

stats.name: Immunity
stats.value: 5 to all damage except corruption or fire damage

effects.effect: The tree of might must be completely destroyed.

At the start of each round while the tree of might is intact, each enemy touching the ground in the encounter area who has M < 0 takes 10 corruption damage, and the tree of might grows a fruit. The potency increases by 1 each subsequent round.

Once per round, any creature adjacent to the tree of might can take a fruit from the tree and eat it (no action required). The creature gains 10 temporary Stamina and has their Might score increased by 1 (to a maximum of 6) until the end of the encounter.

items.name: Arrow Launcher
items.flavor: A small wooden cart uses alchemical rockets to launch up to a hundred arrows at a time across a wide area.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to an arrow launcher can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Arrow Storm** ability.
effects.tier2: The arrow launcher is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The arrow launcher is deactivated and can't be used.

features.name: Arrow Storm
features.target: Each creature and object in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: This ability can't be used again until the arrow launcher is reloaded.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The arrow launcher is reloaded, allowing **Arrow Storm** to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The next use of **Arrow Storm** gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The arrow launcher and the creature using this action move together up to 3 squares.

effects.name: Flaming Arrows
effects.effect: deals fire damage, and can ignite flammable objects in its area.

effects.name: Screamers
effects.effect: The arrows make a high-pitched screaming noise as they are fired and descend onto their targets. The **Screamers** ability replaces **Arrow Storm**.

features.name: Screamers
features.target: Each creature and object in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: This ability can't be used again until the arrow launcher is reloaded.

items.name: Boiling Oil Cauldron
items.flavor: A large cauldron of boiling oil stands ready to be poured onto enemies.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a boiling oil cauldron can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Boiling Oil** ability.
effects.tier2: The boiling oil cauldron is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The boiling oil cauldron is deactivated and can't be used.

features.name: Boiling Oil
features.target: Each creature and object in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: If the boiling oil is poured down on targets from above, it has high ground and gains an edge on the power roll. A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round. This ability can't be used again until the boiling oil cauldron is reloaded.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The boiling oil cauldron is reloaded, allowing **Boiling Oil** to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.

items.name: Catapult
items.flavor: This massive counterweighted engine hurls a heavy projectile for a devastating assault.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a catapult can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Arcing Shot** ability.
effects.tier2: The catapult is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The catapult is deactivated and can't be used.

features.name: Arcing Shot
features.target: Each creature and object in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Line of effect for this ability is an arc that can be traced over obstacles between the catapult and the target area. This ability can't be used again until the catapult is reloaded.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The catapult is reloaded, allowing **Arcing Shot** to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The next use of **Arcing Shot** gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The catapult and the creature using this action move together up to 2 squares.

effects.name: Air Assault
effects.effect: The side fielding the catapult has trained their forces to safely use the siege engine to launch them across the battlefield. As an adjacent creature main action, the catapult can be used to vertical push 10 any ally of size 1L or less. If the ally lands in an unoccupied space, they take no damage.

effects.name: Flammable
effects.effect: deals fire damage, and the area of that ability is on fire until the end of the encounter. Any creature who enters the area for the first time in a round or starts their turn there takes 2 fire damage.

items.name: Exploding Mill Wheel
items.flavor: A massive wooden wheel is loaded with explosives and rolled toward enemy forces or fortifications, ready to explode.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to an exploding mill wheel that isn't rolling can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Roll the Wheel** ability.
effects.tier2: The exploding mill wheel is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The exploding mill wheel is deactivated and can't be used.

effects.effect: Once the wheel is rolling, it can't be deactivated. However, it can be exploded early by destroying it or blocking its movement with a suitably large creature or object.

features.name: Roll the Wheel
features.target: Each creature and object in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: When this ability is used and at the start of every turn thereafter, the exploding mill wheel rolls, moving 2 squares in a straight line. Each creature and object of size 2 or smaller in the area defined by the wheel's movement is targeted by the following power roll. A target force moved this way is moved to either side of the wheel, as the Director determines.

If the wheel enters the space of any creature or object of size 3 or larger, or if it is reduced to 0 Stamina, its movement stops and it explodes. Each creature and object in a 5 burst centered on the wheel is targeted by the following power roll.
A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round.

effects.name: Piloted
effects.effect:
The wheel has been fitted with a control mechanism and a pilot's seat for a creature of size 1M or smaller. As a move action, the pilot can turn the wheel in any direction while it is moving. As a main action, the pilot can leap out of the pilot's seat, landing in an adjacent space while the wheel continues moving in a straight line.
Without proper training, determining how to pilot the wheel requires a **Reason test**.
effects.tier1: The wheel immediately explodes as if striking a size 3 or larger creature or object.
effects.tier2: The creature fails to pilot the wheel.
effects.tier3: The creature can pilot the wheel.

effects.effect: On a natural 19 or 20, a creature can both pilot the wheel and can disarm its explosives as a maneuver.

items.name: Field Ballista
items.flavor: A massive crossbow fires thick metal bolts with devastating effect.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a field ballista can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Release Bolt** ability.
effects.tier2: The field ballista is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The field ballista is deactivated and can't be used.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: This ability can't be used again until the field ballista is reloaded.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The field ballista is reloaded, allowing **Release Bolt** to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The field ballista and the creature using this action move together up to 3 squares.

effects.name: Penetrating Bolt
effects.effect: The field ballista targets the nearest two additional creatures or objects in a straight line beyond the initial target.

effects.name: Chain Bolt
effects.effect:
The field ballista's bolts are set with heavy chains that wrap around targets. The **Chain Bolt** ability replaces **Release Bolt**, and the field ballista gains the **Crank the Chain** ability.
🏹 **Chain Bolt**
| **- - Ranged, Strike, Weapon** | **Main action (Adjacent creature)** |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------: |
| **📏 Ranged 20**               |       **🎯 One creature or object** |

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect:
This ability can't be used again until the field ballista is reloaded.
🏹 **Crank the Chain**
| **Ranged, Strike, Weapon** | **Main action (Adjacent creature)** |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------: |
| **📏 Ranged 20**           |                 **🎯 One creature** |

effects.name: Special
effects.effect: The target must be slowed by the field ballista.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: This forced movement triggers opportunity attacks.

items.name: Iron Dragon
items.flavor: A massive metal device uses a bellows system and liquid fuel to shoot out gouts of flame.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to an iron dragon can make an **Agility test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Gout of Flame** ability.
effects.tier2: The iron dragon is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
effects.tier3: The iron dragon is deactivated and can't be used.

features.name: Gout of Flame
features.target: Each creature and object in the area

effects.tier1: 6 fire damage; A < 0 the target is burning (save ends)
effects.tier2: 10 fire damage; A < 1 the target is burning (save ends)
effects.tier3: 13 fire damage; A < 2 the target is burning (save ends)

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round. This ability can't be used again until the iron dragon is reloaded.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The iron dragon is reloaded, allowing **Gout of Flame** to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The next use of **Gout of Flame** gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The iron dragon and the creature using this action move together up to 2 squares.

items.name: Watchtower
items.flavor: A sturdy wooden tower accessed by interior ladders or stairs provides cover and high ground for attackers.

effects.effect: The watchtower must be completely destroyed.
Creatures who have access to the watchtower's interior ladders or stairs have high ground and cover against creatures outside the watchtower.
A creature outside and adjacent to the watchtower can gain access to the interior by climbing it as an **Agility test** or breaking into it with a **Might test**.
effects.tier1: 1d6 damage; the creature remains outside the watchtower
effects.tier2: The creature remains outside the watchtower.
effects.tier3: The creature gains access to the watchtower.

effects.name: Ballista Emplacement
effects.effect: The watchtower is equipped with a field ballista that can be used by creatures in the watchtower. The ballista can't be moved.

effects.name: Boiling Oil Cauldron
effects.effect: The watchtower is equipped with a boiling oil cauldron that can be used by creatures in the watchtower.

effects.name: Spyglass
effects.effect: Any creature in the watchtower can use the spyglass to search for hidden creatures around the tower, gaining an edge on the Intuition test and increasing the distance at which creatures can be spotted to 15 squares.

effects.name: Stone Tower
effects.effect: The watchtower is reinforced with stone and has 75 Stamina.

effects.name: Iron Tower
effects.effect: The watchtower is reinforced with stone and iron and has 100 Stamina.

items.name: The Black Obelisk
items.flavor: A foreboding obelisk shaped of dark stone harrows the minds and spirits of those around it.

effects.effect: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to the black obelisk can make a **Reason test**.
effects.tier1: The creature accidentally activates the **Your Fears Become Manifest** ability, which gains an edge.
effects.tier2: The creature must make another test to deactivate the obelisk. If they obtain this outcome a second time, they accidentally activate **Your Fears Become Manifest**.
effects.tier3: The obelisk is deactivated until the end of the encounter.

effects.effect: A new round starts.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The **Your Fears Become Manifest** ability.

features.name: Your Fears Become Manifest
features.trigger: A new round starts.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The target is pushed 2 squares.

items.name: The Chronal Hypercube
items.flavor: This unnatural object twists space around it in a reflection of its own unnatural form.

effects.effect: A creature who has the Psionics skill can deactivate and take control of the chronal hypercube by making a **Reason test** while within 10 squares of the hypercube.
effects.tier2: The creature fails to deactivate the hypercube.
effects.tier3: The hypercube teleports adjacent to the creature at the start of the next round and becomes an ally to the creature and their allies.

effects.effect: At the start of each round while the hypercube is present, roll a d10. On a 7 or higher, the hypercube teleports to a square of one ally's choice within 10 squares and is hidden. While the hypercube is hidden, Psionics is the only skill that can be applied to a test made to find it.
Any ally within 10 squares of the hypercube can teleport when they move. An ally who teleports gains an edge on the next power roll they make.

items.name: The Throne of A'An
items.flavor: The throne of A'An, sun god of the Antical Protectorate in what is now Vanigar, retains some of her power from the age before she was slain to end the Age of Suns—and plunge the region into eternal winter.

effects.effect: The throne of A'An can be deactivated only by the current hierophant of A'An (see **Sitting on the Throne**), who must succeed on a **Presence test** that takes a bane to do so.
effects.tier2: The hierophant fails to deactivate the throne.
effects.tier3: The throne is deactivated until the end of the encounter.

effects.effect:
In the Age of Suns, there was no darkness and no night. Even among the many suns of that time, the light of A'An was the brightest. The throne of A'An manifests the sun powers of that god, even when no one is seated in it. The following effects always occur within 10 squares of the throne:

- The throne sheds bright light that negates all darkness and concealment, and which prevents creatures from being hidden.
- Any creature with cold immunity has fire weakness 10.
- Any creature who uses an ability that deals cold damage takes 11 fire damage.
Only a creature attuned to the throne can sit on it. A creature adjacent to the throne can use a main action to attune to it by succeeding on a **Presence test**.
effects.tier2: The creature fails to attune to the throne.
effects.tier3: The creature attunes to the throne and can sit on it.

effects.effect:
A creature seated on the throne becomes the hierophant of A'An and gains the following benefits:

- The hierophant and each of their allies within 10 squares of the throne have fire immunity 10.
- The hierophant and each of their allies within 10 squares of the throne can choose to have their abilities deal fire damage instead of their usual damage.
- The hierophant has a +5 bonus to stability, and any strike made against them takes a bane unless the attacker is also attuned to the throne.
- The hierophant can use the **Primordial Flare** and **Solar Accretion** abilities.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The target has fire weakness 10 until the start of the hierophant's next turn.

features.name: Solar Accretion
features.trigger: A target within distance is made winded or is reduced to 0 Stamina by fire damage.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: If the hierophant is a hero, they gain 3 of their Heroic Resource. If the hierophant is a Director-controlled creature, the Director gains 3 Malice.

features.name: Nova
features.target: Each creature and object in the area
features.trigger: The throne is destroyed or the hierophant obtains a tier 1 outcome on the test to deactivate it.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Each target takes 14 fire damage and the Hierophant gains the Incubator of A'An complication (see the sidebar). If there is no hierophant, one creature within 10 squares of the throne chosen by the Director gains this complication.

items.name: Ajax's Malice
items.flavor: At the start of Ajax's turn, you can spend Malice to activate one of the following features.

effects.effect: Ajax attempts to instill doubt into a creature within line of effect through logic and reason. The creature and Ajax make an opposed Reason test. If Ajax wins, he chooses to either deal 11 extra damage to one target on his next strike or to gain an additional triggered action during the current round. Ajax can't use this feature against the same creature during the same encounter.
Until the end of the round, Ajax chooses one of the following environments he has previously visited and overlays that environment on top of the encounter map, temporarily merging multiple realities.

effects.name: Incredibly High Above the Ground
effects.effect: The winds whip and bluster. Any creature who can't fly takes a −3 penalty to stability, and forced movement effects gain a +3 bonus to their distance against such creatures.

effects.name: Swamp
effects.effect: The ground is difficult terrain for enemies. Any creature who starts and ends their turn in the same space is restrained (save ends).

effects.name: Volcanic Canyon
effects.effect: The air is stiflingly hot. Each enemy takes 5 fire damage for each square they enter.
Ajax takes an additional main action on his turn. He can use this feature even if he is dazed.

features.name: Draw Steel
features.target: Each enemy and object in the area

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Each target makes a test using their highest characteristic.

Ajax then raises his Blade of the Gol King above his head as four giant blades emerge from the ground to fill the area. Each target is pushed into an unoccupied space adjacent to the area after the power roll is resolved. Each blade blocks line of effect and can be dismissed by Ajax at will (no action required).

items.name: Tactical Stance
items.flavor: At the start of each round, Ajax chooses a new stance from one of the following options and gains its benefits:

effects.effect: Ajax automatically treats his initial power roll as a 17. He can still roll to determine if he scores a critical hit.
Before he uses an ability, Ajax can either shift up to 2 squares, or can cause one creature within line of effect to slide up to 2 squares, ignoring stability.
Ajax has damage immunity 5. Additionally, any enemy who makes a power roll that includes Ajax as a target has a double bane on the roll.

effects.name: Ajax Turns
effects.effect: Ajax takes up to three turns each round. He can't take turns consecutively. Additionally, he can use three triggered actions in a round while he isn't dazed.

effects.name: End Effect
effects.effect: At the end of each of his turns, Ajax can take 20 damage to end up to two effects on him that can be ended by a saving throw. This damage can't be reduced in any way.

effects.tier1: 16 damage; M < 4 the target loses 1d3 Recoveries
effects.tier2: 22 damage; M < 5 the target loses 1d3 Recoveries
effects.tier3: 26 damage; M < 6 prone and the target loses 1d3 Recoveries

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax shifts up to 2 squares between striking each target.
Ajax can strike one additional target for each Malice spent.

features.name: Decree by the Jade Hand
features.target: Each enemy and object in the area

effects.tier1: 11 holy damage; slide 2; P < 4 the target is hexed (save ends)
effects.tier2: 17 holy damage; slide 5; P < 5 the target is hexed (save ends)
effects.tier3: 21 holy damage; slide 8; P < 6 the target is hexed (save ends)

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: A hexed target glows green, and each of their heroic abilities has its cost increased by 2.
The potency increases by 1. Additionally, the ground beneath the area drops 3 squares and is difficult terrain. Each flying target who has M < 5 is knocked prone.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: If the target is grabbed, Ajax can choose to keep the vine extended, pull the target adjacent to him, or pull himself adjacent to the target. The vine stays attached to a grabbed target until it takes damage from a strike, the target escapes the grab, or Ajax causes the vine to release the target (no action required).

effects.name: Special
effects.effect: This ability can be replaced with the features of a different treasure Ajax has acquired.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax throws a glowing bead to a square within distance, which ignites at the start of Ajax's next turn and creates an area around it that lasts until the start of Ajax's following turn. Each enemy in the area when the bead ignites takes 20 fire damage, and if they have A < 5, they are dazed (save ends). Any enemy who starts their turn in the area takes 10 fire damage.

Ajax dies only when his Stamina reaches −350. While his Stamina is below 0, Ajax is bleeding, he can choose any two options from his Tactical Stance trait each round, and the Director gains 2 additional Malice per round.

features.name: Is This What They Taught You?
features.trigger: A creature within distance marks Ajax.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The target is marked while Ajax is marked. While the target is marked this way, Ajax gains an edge on power rolls against them, and whenever the target uses a triggered action involving their mark on Ajax, he can make a free strike against them.

features.name: Shieldbreaker Talisman
features.trigger: An enemy within distance uses an ability to reduce damage.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax makes a free strike against the target, dealing extra damage equal to twice the amount that was reduced. This extra damage can't be reduced in any way.

features.name: Who's Hesitating?
features.trigger: A creature uses the Hesitation is Weakness ability.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax shifts up to his speed and can make a free strike. If the target has R < 4, this free strike also makes them weakened until the end of their next turn.

features.name: Your Obsession With Me Betrays You
features.trigger: Ajax causes a creature within distance to gain ferocity or wrath.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: If the target has I < 4, they use a signature ability against a target of Ajax's choice.

features.name: You Would Flounder Your Assault?
features.trigger: A creature within 10 squares regains Stamina.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax regains the same amount of Stamina.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax flies at high speed to cut through each target, then appears in an unoccupied space within distance.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Ajax uses the shadow elf eclipse's technique to reduce each target's surges to 0. Additionally, until the end of the round, Ajax ignores edges and double edges on any target's abilities, and ignores any nondamaging effects of any target's damage-dealing abilities.

effects.name: Special
effects.effect: This villain action can be replaced with a villain action from a creature any target has previously encountered.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: Each target who has I < 5 is knocked prone and can't stand until Ajax deals damage to them. For each target not knocked prone, Ajax can move up to his speed toward that target and use Blade of the Gol King against them.

items.name: Angulotl Malice
items.flavor: At the start of any angulotl's turn, you can spend Malice to activate one of the following features.

effects.effect: Until the end of the round, when an angulotl moves through an inactive angulotl's space, the inactive angulotl can use a free triggered action to jump 3 squares.
Each angulotl in the encounter puffs out their throat and starts loudly droning. Any non-angulotl adjacent to an angulotl makes an **Intuition test.**
An angulotl calls clouds to cover the encounter map and unleash rain until the end of the round. Any creature or object that is exposed to the sky is wet until the end of the encounter.

features.name: Hop and Chop
features.target: One creature or object per minion

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The cleaver jumps up to 4 squares before or after making this strike.
Whenever an adjacent enemy grabs the cleaver or uses a melee ability against them, that enemy takes 1 poison damage.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The dart gains an edge on this ability against any target who has less than full Stamina.
Whenever an adjacent enemy grabs the dart or uses a melee ability against them, that enemy takes 1 poison damage.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The next time the target makes a strike against the daybringer, the target takes 4 acid damage after the strike is resolved.
The daybringer jumps up to 3 squares before or after using this ability.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The daybringer expands their throat to make it resemble the sun until the start of their next turn. During that time, each angulotl who starts their turn within 10 squares of the daybringer regains 5 Stamina and gains a +3 bonus to speed until the end of their turn.

features.name: Tongue Slap
features.trigger: The target makes a strike against the daybringer or an ally that isn't a critical hit.

effects.name: Effect

effects.effect: An illuminated creature or object can't hide or become invisible, and any strike made against an illuminated target gains an edge.

effects.tier3: 1 poison damage; the target is wet (EoT)

items.flavor: At the start of an arixx's turn, you can spend Malice to activate one of the following features.

items.name: Ashen Hoarder Malice
items.flavor: At the start of an ashen hoarder's turn, you can spend Malice to activate one of the following features.

effects.effect: The ashen hoarder moves up to their speed and can make a free strike against two targets.

The ashen hoarder summons a 10 wall of bones and blades into unoccupied squares within 5 squares of them. Each square of the wall has 5 Stamina. An enemy who comes adjacent to the wall for the first time in a round or starts their turn there takes 3 damage.
The ashen hoarder takes an additional main action on their turn. They can use this feature even if they are dazed.

The ashen hoarder launches bone lances into the air, raining them down on enemies and impaling those unlucky enough to be on the receiving end. Each enemy within 20 squares of the ashen hoarder makes an **Agility test**.

effects.tier2: 15 damage; if one target has M < 3 they are bleeding (save ends); if the other target has A < 3 they are grabbed
effects.tier3: 18 damage; M < 4 bleeding (save ends); A < 2 grabbed

effects.tier2: 11 corruption damage; M < 3 the target is impaled (save ends)
effects.tier3: 14 corruption damage; M < 4 the target is impaled (save ends)

Each creature or object in the path of this movement is either pushed into the nearest unoccupied space outside the path, or if they have M < 3 is pushed forward until the movement ends. Any creature who is force moved forward into an obstacle is dazed (save ends).

features.trigger: The ashen hoarder takes damage.

An adjacent enemy who grabs the ashen hoarder or uses a melee ability against them takes 3 damage.

When the ashen hoarder is reduced to 0 Stamina, they explode in a swirling singularity of bone shards and soul energy. Each creature within 5 squares of the ashen hoarder who has M < 3 takes 11 corruption damage. A creature killed by this damage has their soul sucked into the vortex and lost somewhere in the Abyssal Wasteland, and can't be brought back to life until their soul is recovered.

effects.name: Effect
effects.effect: The ashen hoarder moves up to their speed and uses Claw and Blade with a double edge against one target. On a tier 3 outcome, the ashen hoarder can use Impale without spending Malice.

items.name: Bredbeddle Malice
items.flavor: At the start of a bredbeddle's turn, you can spend Malice to activate one of the following features.

effects.effect: The bredbeddle's axe lengthens and turns a ghastly green, granting a +1 bonus to the distance of the bredbeddle's melee strikes and the dimensions of their burst area abilities until the end of their turn.

A ghostly size 1L stockade seeps out from under the bredbeddle's feet to fill an unoccupied square within 10 squares. When a size 1L or smaller enemy enters the stockade's square, they are restrained (save ends). When a restrained creature is no longer restrained, the stockade fades away. At the start of each of the bredbeddle's turns, they can slide an active stockade and any creature in it up to 5 squares.
The bredbeddle takes an additional main action on their turn. They can use this feature even if they are dazed.

A phantom second bredbeddle phases into view, appearing in an unoccupied space anywhere on the encounter map, then vanishing at the end of the round. The phantom bredbeddle shares the original bredbeddle's statistics but has 24 Stamina, corruption immunity 10, and can fly. The phantom bredbeddle can take one turn and use any of the bredbeddle's abilities except for villain actions. Only one phantom bredbeddle can be active at a time.

effects.name: End Effect
effects.effect: At the end of each of their turns, the bredbeddle can take 5 damage to end one effect on them that can be ended by a saving throw. This damage can't be reduced in any way.

While headless, the bredbeddle can move into a space containing a severed head and attach it to their neck as a main action. Doing so physically transforms the bredbeddle, who takes on the appearance, size, weight, and stability of the head's original owner. If the bredbeddle takes the form of a creature of size 1L or smaller, the distance of their melee and burst area abilities decreases by 1. These effects last until the bredbeddle is killed or beheaded, or until the head falls off after 24 hours. A head that falls off this way can no longer be attached to this bredbeddle.

A creature must succeed on a **hard Might test** made as a maneuver to rip a head off the bredbeddle. If they fail, the bredbeddle can make a free strike against them.
The bredbeddle can't be physically transformed in any way except by their Heady or Not trait.

effects.effect: The werewolf can take two turns each round. They can't take turns consecutively.

The werewolf's ferocity is expressed through rage, and their abilities can inflict rage points on any enemy except a stormwight fury. A creature who starts their turn with 10 or more rage expends their rage. Then before taking their turn, they must shift up to their speed toward the nearest creature and make a melee free strike against them. A creature who takes damage from this free strike gains 1 rage. Accumulated rage disappears after a character finishes a respite.
The werewolf enters combat in their hybrid humanoid form. Their shape can't be changed by any external effect.
The werewolf ignores difficult terrain.

If the target has P < 0, they are afflicted with lycanthpy. Each time the target is unaffected by the potency effect, the potency increases by 1 the next time the werewolf uses the ability against the same target. A creature afflicted with lycanthropy gains 2 rage at the end of each of their turns whenever they're in combat. Their rage doesn't disappear after finishing a respite and they must complete the Find a Cure downtime project in "Draw Steel: Heroes" to end this effect.
